decisions.reason: The quantified comparison in step 1.3 is false for an unbounded compactly supported kernel: in dimension one, phi(z)=|z|^(-1)1_{0<|z|<=1} and F=1 have an infinite Euclidean integral but finite sphere integral. This is nonfatal for the stated equivalence because its only applications are the bounded smooth densities rho and psi. Added boundedness and Borel measurability, the explicit bound M R^d/d, and exact uncompleted-Tonelli and translation-invariance suppliers; both comparisons remain valid for extended integrals.

F1 incorrectly infers Sobolev membership from almost-everywhere equality alone, and omits p-integrability from the Lp quotient. Repaired F1 to require an Lp class already in W^{k,p}, and made step 1.1 explicitly use the zero class, whose weak derivatives all vanish. The actual witnesses restrict identically to zero in the ball, so their common Sobolev trace is zero despite different boundary restrictions. The independent radial witness remains in L2 by the computed integrable (1-r)^(-1/2) bound and diverges toward every boundary point. This is a nonfatal overstatement of a fact, not a failed witness.

Clause (ii) inaccurately calls the published definition uniform: it specifies only local one-sided graphs and derivative bounds on compact patches, explicitly denying uniform chart constants. Replaced that wording by the exact local graph condition and explained that a finite shrunk cover yields domain-dependent bounds. Corrected the cusp explanation: the tip fails the graph condition, while individual arcs may be C1; the planar companion computation fails for alpha>p. The positive trace, sharp-range, right-inverse and kernel clauses match their actual suppliers; endpoint assertions remain explicitly attributed and unproved. This is a nonfatal scope-description defect, not an invalid trace theorem.

repair_notes.source_evidence: Read the full published domain definition and all five positive-result interfaces, the home pages and the actual planar cusp statement. Retrieved complete Mironescu (186529 bytes), Gagliardo (1360343 bytes), and Zuppa (133895 bytes) PDFs by Python HTTP client after browser-tool failures. Read Mironescu Section 1 through the complete Theorem 1.2 proof and Section 2 endpoint paragraph: a smooth L1 summable decomposition and datum-dependent shrinking normal cutoff yield a W11 lift, not a linear right inverse. Read Gagliardo printed pp. 285 and 290: bounded locally Lipschitz one-sided domains and Teorema 1.II. Read Hajlasz-Martio printed p.243 remark (4), which is explicitly a hyperplane result. Read Kazaniecki-Wojciechowski introduction and complete Section 2 proof: a hypothetical right inverse embeds nonatomic L1 in a countable weighted l1 space via the BV cell-average projection, contradicting the l1 embedding obstruction. Its formal Theorem 1 is planar; the introduction explains localization to Lipschitz boundaries and p.3 notes the higher-dimensional extension. Read Zuppa pp.23-25: weighted estimates and sufficient compactness for its R3 Qk,alpha models under Condition A1; no necessity of weights or universal cusp threshold was inferred.
